llm.reply:
The KRAS gene product is a small GTPase belonging to the Kirsten ras oncogene family [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. A single amino acid substitution can switch it into an activated, transforming form [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. The findings describe its activity through its protein family and its downstream signalling, but give no more detailed biochemical description.

## Oncogenic Activation

The activated protein is implicated in several cancers [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. Alternative splicing produces two isoforms [11: "variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].

## Downstream Signalling

KRAS-dependent gene transcription in mutant cancers runs mainly through the ERK MAPK cascade [29: "is driven predominantly through the ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade"]. In pancreatic cancer, KRAS activity depends on the exchange factor SOS1 [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"].

## Therapeutic Targeting

KRAS was long considered hard to drug [26: "KRAS has been deemed a challenging therapeutic target, even \"undruggable\""]. The G12C mutant form has since been targeted with covalent inhibitors [30: "glycine at position 12 with cysteine (G12C), which is clinically drugged through covalent inhibitors"]. Degrader molecules affect many mutant forms of the protein [30: "potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"].

The KRAS gene product is a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The OMIM record is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. A single residue change can activate it [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## Gene Identity

The gene symbol is KRAS [1]. The gene name is KRAS [5]. The literature entity name is Kras [6]. Splicing produces two protein forms [11: "two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].

## Signalling And Oncogenesis

KRAS-dependent transcription runs mainly through ERK [29: "is driven predominantly through the ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade"]. One paper is Defining the KRAS- and ERK-dependent transcriptome in KRAS-mutant cancers. [18]. Oncogenic KRAS acts on fibroblasts in colorectal cancer [27: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2)"]. That paper is Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression. [9]. The activated protein is linked to several cancers [11: "lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"].

## Therapeutic Targeting

KRAS was long considered hard to drug [26: "KRAS has been deemed a challenging therapeutic target, even \"undruggable\""]. A related review is KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer. [2]. Upstream exchange-factor inhibition is one indirect approach [28: "inhibition of the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. Another paper is Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer. [14]. Degraders act on many alleles [30: "degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. That paper is Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders. [22]. Related PMIDs include 34776511 [8]. Another is 37768068 [13]. Another is 38686056 [17]. Another is 38843331 [21]. Another is 39298590 [25].

## Variants And Trials

One ClinVar record is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. Another is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23]. One trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Another is A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Another is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Another is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
